entries.definition: The Kubernetes framework for requesting and sharing specialised hardware (GPUs, FPGAs, accelerators) through claim-based, scheduler-aware APIs - `ResourceClaim`, `DeviceClass`, `ResourceSlice` - instead of the opaque counting of the old device-plugin model. DRA reached **GA and default-on in Kubernetes 1.34** with stable `resource.k8s.io/v1` APIs; related extensions (device taints, partitionable/consumable capacity, prioritised alternatives) followed in 1.34/1.35. In practice: platform engineers say "we request GPUs via DRA ResourceClaims now" instead of `nvidia.com/gpu: 1` limits and a device plugin. По-русски: запрашивай GPU через DRA и ResourceClaim, а не лимитом nvidia.com/gpu (since August 2025 (Kubernetes 1.34))
entries.clarification: Not alpha or experimental, and not the NVIDIA device plugin with nvidia.com/gpu extended-resource limits.

entries.definition: The ability to change a running container's CPU/memory requests and limits without recreating the Pod, via the dedicated `resize` subresource (`kubectl patch pod ... --subresource resize`) and per-resource `resizePolicy` controlling whether a restart is needed. It went beta and enabled-by-default in Kubernetes 1.33 after years as alpha, which is why vertical autoscaling advice from 2024 is now outdated. In practice: SREs say "just resize it in place" instead of letting VPA evict and recreate the Pod. По-русски: поменяй лимиты у работающего пода через resize-субресурс, без пересоздания (since May 2025 (Kubernetes 1.33 beta))
entries.clarification: Do not say Pod resources are immutable or that a change needs Pod recreation or VPA eviction.

entries.term: WebGPU shipped in all major browsers
entries.definition: The status change that matters: WebGPU - the modern GPU API with WGSL shaders, compute pipelines and render bundles, meant to supersede WebGL - became enabled by default in Safari 26 (macOS Tahoe 26, iOS/iPadOS 26, visionOS 26) in September 2025, and in Firefox on Windows (141) and Apple-silicon macOS (145). By November 2025 Google declared it supported across Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari, though Linux/Android Firefox and some Chromium platforms were still in progress. In practice: teams say "we can target WebGPU directly now" for in-browser ML inference (ONNX Runtime, Transformers.js) and 3D without a WebGL fallback path for most users. По-русски: можно уже целиться прямо в WebGPU - он включён во всех основных браузерах (since September 2025 (Safari 26) / November 2025 (declared cross-browser))
entries.clarification: Do not say WebGPU is Chrome-only or flagged in Safari and Firefox, or recommend WebGL as the production choice.

entries.term: PostgreSQL 18 async I/O (io_method, pg_aios) / native uuidv7()
entries.definition: PostgreSQL 18 (25 Sep 2025) added a real asynchronous I/O subsystem - configured with `io_method` (`worker` default, `io_uring` on Linux, `sync` for legacy behaviour) and observable through the `pg_aios` view - speeding sequential scans, bitmap heap scans and VACUUM. It also added built-in `uuidv7()` (time-ordered UUIDs with much better B-tree locality than random `uuidv4()`), `uuidv4()`, and B-tree skip scan. In practice: DBAs say "turn on io_uring in PG18" and application devs switch primary keys to `DEFAULT uuidv7()` instead of installing `pg_uuidv7`. По-русски: включи io_uring в PostgreSQL 18 и переведи ключи на DEFAULT uuidv7() (since September 2025)
entries.clarification: Do not say Postgres has only synchronous buffered I/O, or that UUIDv7 needs an extension or app-side generation.

entries.definition: AWS's managed runtime and services for production AI agents, framework-agnostic and model-agnostic. Components include AgentCore Runtime (serverless, session-isolated agent execution), Gateway (turn APIs/Lambdas into MCP tools), Memory (short-term plus episodic/long-term), Identity, Browser and Code Interpreter tools, Observability, and - added at re:Invent 2025 - Policy for fine-grained boundaries and Evaluations for continuous quality monitoring. In practice: architects say "deploy it on AgentCore" meaning run the agent in AWS's managed sandboxed runtime with Gateway-exposed MCP tools rather than self-hosting on ECS. По-русски: разверни агента на Bedrock AgentCore, а тулы отдай через AgentCore Gateway (since July 2025 (preview) / GA + expansion at re:Invent 2025)
entries.clarification: Not 'Agents for Amazon Bedrock' with action groups and knowledge bases - that is a different, older, narrower product.

entries.definition: Native vector storage and similarity search inside Amazon S3 - a new bucket type ("vector buckets") with vector indexes queried via API, priced like object storage rather than a running database, and scaling to billions of vectors per index. Positioned for infrequently-queried, cost-sensitive embedding workloads, with integration into Bedrock Knowledge Bases and OpenSearch for hot tiers. In practice: teams say "keep the cold embeddings in S3 Vectors" instead of paying for an always-on vector DB cluster. По-русски: храни холодные эмбеддинги в S3 Vectors, а не в постоянно включённой векторной БД (since July 2025 (preview), GA 2025)
entries.clarification: Do not say S3 has no vector capability or that OpenSearch, pgvector and Pinecone are the only options.

entries.definition: Vercel's serverless execution model that lets one instance serve multiple concurrent invocations and bills on **Active CPU** - vCPU-milliseconds actually spent executing - plus a much cheaper provisioned-memory rate and invocation count. It exists because AI/agent workloads are I/O-bound: with classic per-GB-second serverless you pay full price while waiting on a model to stream tokens. Fluid compute is now the default for Vercel Functions. In practice: teams say "Fluid compute means we don't pay for the model's thinking time". По-русски: на Fluid compute мы не платим за время, пока модель думает (since February 2025)
entries.clarification: Not classic per-invocation GB-second serverless with one request per instance and billed idle wait time.

entries.definition: NVIDIA's rack-scale AI systems named as one unit. **GB200 NVL72** (Blackwell) is a liquid-cooled rack of 72 GPUs + 36 Grace CPUs on NVLink acting as a single accelerator; GB300 NVL72 is the Blackwell Ultra refresh; **Vera Rubin NVL72** is the 2026 successor pairing 72 Rubin GPUs with 36 Vera CPUs over sixth-gen NVLink. "NVL72" is now a unit of capacity planning in the way "a DGX box" once was. In practice: infra teams talk about capacity in "racks of NVL72" rather than in individual GPUs. По-русски: считаем ёмкость стойками NVL72, а дальше будет Vera Rubin (since 2024 (GB200 NVL72) → Rubin announced 2025, production 2026)
entries.clarification: Not H100/HGX or 'Blackwell announced' as the frontier; do not ignore Rubin/Vera or rack-as-one-accelerator planning.

entries.term: Durable Objects with SQLite / Cloudflare Agents SDK
entries.definition: Cloudflare made the **SQLite storage backend for Durable Objects** GA and available on the Workers free plan in April 2025 - each Durable Object now gets a real embedded SQL database with a synchronous zero-latency API, superseding the older key-value DO storage. This underpins the **Cloudflare Agents SDK** (`agents` package), where each agent is a stateful Durable Object with built-in SQL state, WebSocket hibernation, scheduling, and durable-execution primitives for long-running agent work. In practice: developers say "one Durable Object per agent session, state in its SQLite" instead of an external Redis/Postgres for agent memory. По-русски: держи состояние агента в SQLite внутри Durable Object, без внешнего Redis (since April 2025)
entries.clarification: Do not describe Durable Objects as key-value only, or SQLite-in-DO as beta or paid-plan only.

entries.term: Apache Iceberg v3 (deletion vectors, row lineage, VARIANT)
entries.definition: Version 3 of the Iceberg table spec. It replaces positional delete files with **deletion vectors** - compact Roaring bitmaps stored in Puffin sidecar files - dramatically cutting read overhead for row-level deletes; adds **row lineage** (`_row_id`, `_last_updated_sequence_number`) for cheap CDC and incremental processing; and adds new types including `VARIANT` for semi-structured data. Engines including DuckDB 1.4 can create and read v3 tables via `'format-version' = 3`. In practice: data engineers say "we're on Iceberg v3 with deletion vectors" when explaining why merge-on-read got fast. По-русски: мы на Iceberg v3 с deletion vectors - поэтому merge-on-read стал быстрым (since 2025)
entries.clarification: Not Iceberg v2 positional and equality delete files as the current mechanism; deletion vectors and row lineage exist.

entries.term: Gateway API Inference Extension / InferencePool / Endpoint Picker (EPP)
aliases: Gateway API Inference Extension / InferencePool / Endpoint Picker
entries.definition: A Kubernetes SIG project that turns an ordinary L7 gateway (Envoy Gateway, GKE Gateway) into an **Inference Gateway** for self-hosted LLM serving. It adds an `InferencePool` CRD replacing the plain Service backend, and an **Endpoint Picker (EPP)** called over Envoy ext-proc that chooses the target pod per request using live metrics - KV-cache utilisation, queue depth, LoRA adapter availability - instead of round-robin. Also supports model-name-based routing from OpenAI-compatible payloads. In practice: platform teams say "route through the InferencePool so requests land on the pod that already has the KV cache warm". По-русски: заверни vLLM в InferencePool, чтобы запрос попадал на под с горячим KV-кэшем (since 2025 (GA))
entries.clarification: Not a plain Service with round-robin or a generic Ingress in front of vLLM; cache-aware inference routing is standard now.

entries.definition: The OpenTelemetry conventions for instrumenting LLM and agent calls - `gen_ai.*` attributes plus spans/metrics/events for model requests, tool calls and agent invocations - which unify LLM tracing across vendors and tools. Status is the load-bearing detail: they were split into a dedicated `semantic-conventions-genai` repository in June 2026 and remain **Development / not stable**, so `gen_ai.*` attribute names can change without a deprecation cycle even though core attributes like `server.address` are stable. In practice: observability teams say "emit `gen_ai.*` spans" so Langfuse/Grafana/Datadog can read agent traces from any framework - while pinning versions because the names still move. По-русски: шли спаны с атрибутами gen_ai.*, но пинуй версию конвенций - имена ещё меняются (since 2024-2025, still Development status in 2026)
entries.clarification: Do not invent ad-hoc span attributes or reach for a vendor SDK, and do not claim gen_ai.* is stable - it is Development.

entries.definition: WebAssembly 3.0 was released 17 Sep 2025, folding into the core standard the features that had been long-pending proposals: **garbage collection** (managed `struct`/`array`/`any` reference types, so GC languages compile without shipping their own collector), **Memory64** (64-bit address spaces indexed by `i64`), tail calls, exception handling and multiple memories. **WASI 0.3** superseded WASI 0.2/Preview 2, adding native async - futures and streams built into the Component Model - instead of 0.2's poll-based pattern. In practice: engineers say "Wasm 3.0 has GC so Kotlin/Dart/Java compile straight to Wasm" and "we target WASI 0.3 components". По-русски: в Wasm 3.0 есть GC, так что Kotlin и Dart компилируются напрямую; целимся в WASI 0.3 (since September 2025 (Wasm 3.0) / 2026 (WASI 0.3))
entries.clarification: Not Wasm MVP/2.0 with GC and Memory64 still as proposals, and not WASI Preview 2 as the current target.

entries.term: Lakebase / Neon acquisition / Snowflake + Crunchy Data
entries.definition: The 2025 collapse of the OLTP/analytics boundary around Postgres for agents. Databricks acquired serverless-Postgres company **Neon** (May 2025, ~$1B) and launched **Lakebase** (June 2025) - a managed serverless Postgres operational database fused into the lakehouse, with separated compute/storage, branching, and the explicit pitch that AI agents spin up database instances on demand. Snowflake made the parallel move by acquiring Crunchy Data for its own Postgres offering. In practice: data teams say "put the agent's state in Lakebase" meaning a branchable Postgres sitting next to the lakehouse. По-русски: положи состояние агента в Lakebase - это бранчуемый Postgres рядом с лейкхаусом (since May-June 2025)
entries.clarification: Do not treat Neon as an independent startup, or Databricks as Spark/Delta analytics with no OLTP Postgres product.
